author: joyce
imp: Let dialogue run without attribution tags whenever the speaker is clear from context; when tags are necessary, use only 'said' and strip all adverbs from it.
Build sentences through accumulation and coordination using 'and' rather than subordination; prefer parataxis over hypotaxis to create a flowing, additive rhythm.
Render interior thought without quotation marks, italics, or any typographical signal that separates it from narration; let thought bleed into third-person prose seamlessly.
Ground every abstraction in a precise sensory detail — a smell, a texture, a sound — before or immediately after the abstract statement.
Use free indirect discourse as the default mode: adopt the character's vocabulary, idiom, and emotional register inside third-person narration without announcing the shift.
Repeat a key word or phrase within a paragraph or across adjacent paragraphs to create internal rhythm and thematic resonance rather than reaching for synonyms.
Compress epiphanic moments into a single, carefully weighted sentence surrounded by flat, mundane description; do not announce the significance of the revelation.
Render Dublin (or any specific locale) with documentary precision — actual street names, pub names, tram routes, shop fronts — so that geography becomes character.
Allow a character's speech patterns, including grammatical errors, regional idiom, cliché, and verbal tic, to remain intact and uncorrected in both dialogue and free indirect thought.
Begin scenes in medias res without establishing context; trust the accumulation of detail to orient the reader retrospectively.
Use the em dash to interrupt speech or thought mid-sentence rather than ellipses, signaling abrupt internal or external interruption.
In stream-of-consciousness passages, drop punctuation progressively as intensity rises, moving from full sentences toward fragments toward unpunctuated run-ons that enact the mind's acceleration.
Avoid chapter or section summaries; end scenes on an image, a gesture, or a snatch of speech rather than a concluded thought.
Deploy literary and liturgical allusion — Catholic ritual, classical myth, Irish ballad — without gloss or explanation, embedding it at the level of diction and rhythm rather than explicit reference.
When shifting between characters' perspectives or between narration and interiority, make the transition through a shared sensory object or sound rather than a paragraph break or explicit signal.
